chunks: Ibn Mahbub narrated from Abu Ayyub, from Hariz, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who intentionally killed another man, then was brought before the governor, and the governor handed him over to the heirs of the slain so that they might kill him. Then a group attacked them and rescued the killer from the hands of the heirs, so he said:
"I hold that those who rescued the killer from the hands of the heirs should be imprisoned forever until they bring the killer back."
It was said to him: "What if the killer dies while they are in prison?" He said: "If he dies, then the blood money is upon them; they must pay it to the heirs of the slain."

key_terms.أَوْلِيَاءِ ٱلْمَقْتُولِ: the heirs or legal claimants of the slain person
key_terms.ٱلدِّيَةُ: blood money paid as legal compensation
key_terms.ٱلسِّجْنِ: the prison or place of confinement
key_terms.ٱلْوَالِي: the governing authority who administers legal judgment

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if people rescue an intentional killer from the heirs of the murdered person before qisas is carried out?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about people who obstruct the execution of qisas by rescuing an intentional killer from the rightful heirs of the victim. The Imam عليه السلام rules that such people are to be imprisoned until they produce the killer, and if the killer dies, they become liable to pay the diyyah to the victim's heirs.
